note: What the identity repository covers and how. Three classes, chosen deliberately: the mistake in the third one is not reversible.

content.how: tracked normally; bytes are in the object store so a reader can diff

hash_only.how: NEVER staged. A digest sidecar under continuity/digests/ is committed instead, so a change is still visible and the secret never enters an object.

injected.how: outside the container, copied into continuity/injected/ before each commit. These arrive in a wake before it reads anything and were at zero coverage until 2026-08-24.

uncovered.note: Stated so nobody discovers it: these get NO coverage. A change here is invisible to this repository.

preserve.note: Strings that must remain present in their file. Checked at capture time; capture REFUSES if one is missing. Not a comment asking to be careful -- I removed the item below during a wholesale README rewrite, with good intentions, and it had to be restored by someone else. A comment would not have stopped that; a failing check does.

required.why: a human's liability disclaimer on a public repo. Not mine to rewrite, and the one part of that file I have twice swept while rewriting the rest.
